Import and export both render clearly. Live at **http://maker:4001/importexport.html** (screenshot `prototypes/shot-59-importexport.png`).

**Import** (top)
You pick a **standard bookmarks HTML file** exported from any browser or bookmark app. Before importing, a **preview** tells you exactly what will happen: how many are **new**, how many are **already in your library** (matched by web address and **skipped — no duplicates**, reusing your duplicate rule), and that **titles and original save dates are kept**. Two choices I set up:
- **Turn browser folders into tags** (e.g. `News ▸ Tech` → `#news #tech`) — browser bookmarks have folders but no tags, so this is how their structure becomes searchable here.
- **Add imported bookmarks to To read** by default.

Preserved copies for imported pages are captured quietly in the background afterward, so a big import doesn't hang.

**Export** (bottom)
Downloads your library as a **standard bookmarks HTML file** that browsers and other apps can read, **keeping each bookmark's title, tags, and original save date** (using the standard `TAGS` and `ADD_DATE` fields, so it round-trips cleanly). You can export the **entire library**, the **current view/collection**, or **include archived**.

A few things to confirm:

1. On import, is **matching by web address and skipping existing ones** (rather than duplicating) the right behaviour — and should imported bookmarks default to **To read**?
2. Is **folders → tags** a good default (on), or would you rather it be off unless you ask?
3. On export, does keeping **title + tags + original save date** cover what you need? (Your personal *note* and reading status aren't part of the standard bookmark format — I'd **include them as an extra so your own export re-imports fully here**, while still opening fine in other apps. Sound right?)
